english.title: Aid / abet a failure to comply with regulations in respect of management of housing in multiple occupation
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) aided, abetted, counselled or procured another, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), to fail to comply with **(..SPECIFY THE REGULATIONS..) made in respect of a house which was in multiple occupation in that **(..SPECIFY THE BREACH..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 234 of the Housing Act 2004 and and section 44 of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 234(4) of the Housing Act 2004.provides that in proceedings against a person for an offence under subsection (3) it is a defence that he had a reasonable excuse for not complying with the regulation.

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit on prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
